public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 682

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/682](https://www.erdosproblems.com/682)
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar.
  (1979), 71-80.
- [GaTa25] A. Gafni and T. Tao, Rough numbers between consecutive primes. arXiv:2508.06463 (2025).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics

namespace Erdos682

/-- The `n`th prime, indexed from zero: `p 0 = 2`, `p 1 = 3`, ... -/
noncomputable abbrev p (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.nth Nat.Prime n

/--
Is it true that for almost all $n$ there exists some $m\in (p_n,p_{n+1})$ such that
$$p(m) \geq p_{n+1}-p_n,$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?

This was solved in the affirmative by Gafni and Tao [GaTa25].

This was formalized in Lean by Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos682.lean#L5018"]
theorem erdos_682 : answer(True) ↔
    {n | ∃ m ∈ Set.Ioo (p n) (p (n + 1)), p (n + 1) - p n ≤ m.minFac}.HasDensity 1 := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Gafni and Tao [GaTa25] proved that the number of exceptional $n\in [1,X]$ is
$$\ll \frac{X}{(\log X)^2}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_682.variants.exceptional_count :
    (fun X : ℕ ↦ ({n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 X |
        ∀ m ∈ Set.Ioo (p n) (p (n + 1)), m.minFac < p (n + 1) - p n}.card : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun X : ℕ ↦ (X : ℝ) / Real.log X ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős first thought this should be true for all large $n$, but found a (conditional)
counterexample: Dickson's conjecture says there are infinitely many $d$ such that
$$2183+30030d\textrm{ and }2201+30030d$$
are both prime, and then they must necessarily be consecutive primes. These give a counterexample
since $30030=2\cdot 3 \cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13$ and every integer in $[2184,2200]$ is
divisible by at least one of these primes.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos682.lean#L5222"]
theorem erdos_682.variants.dickson_counterexample (d : ℕ) (h₁ : (2183 + 30030 * d).Prime)
    (h₂ : (2201 + 30030 * d).Prime) : ∃ n, p n = 2183 + 30030 * d ∧ p (n + 1) = 2201 + 30030 * d ∧
      ∀ m ∈ Set.Ioo (p n) (p (n + 1)), m.minFac < p (n + 1) - p n := by
  sorry

end Erdos682

findings.description: The count in lines 60–62 is over prime-gap indices 1 ≤ n ≤ X, but the asserted O(X / (log X)^2) bound belongs to the prime-value scale, not the index scale. Gafni–Tao count exceptional gaps whose lower prime p_n lies in [X, 2X]. For the first N gaps, their result gives O(N / log N) exceptions. Thus the Lean statement is stronger by a logarithmic factor, not an equivalent reindexing. It is also incompatible with the paper's conditional asymptotic c N / log N for the index count. The docstring repeats the same error.
findings.source_evidence: Gafni–Tao, Rough numbers between consecutive primes, arXiv:2508.06463, Theorem 1.1: “For X>2, let N(X) be the number of prime gaps ... with p_n ∈ [X,2X]” that contain no rough number; then N(X) ≪ X/log²X. The paragraph immediately following explicitly bounds the proportion among the first N gaps by O(1/log N), and conditionally gives asymptotic c/log N. https://arxiv.org/e-print/2508.06463 . The summary at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/682 currently repeats the erroneous index-scale bound, so this discrepancy is inherited from that summary; the cited primary paper is unambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the existing index count and replace `(X : ℝ) / Real.log X ^ 2` with `(X : ℝ) / Real.log X`, updating the docstring accordingly. Alternatively, retain the squared logarithm and count exceptional n with `p n ∈ Set.Icc X (2 * X)`, using `Finset.range (2 * X)` as a finite indexing superset.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the weak inequality p(m) ≥ p_{n+1} − p_n, matching the current webpage and Gafni–Tao. Erdős's final density-zero sentence on p. 74 instead uses the strict inequality >.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two good-gap predicates differ only for twin-prime gaps: outside the initial empty gap, prime gaps are even, and a least prime factor can equal the gap length only when that length is 2. Standard sieve bounds give O(N/log N) twin-prime gaps among the first N gaps, hence their indices have density zero. Consequently the weak and strict versions have density one simultaneously. Gafni–Tao explicitly discuss this distinction in the first remark following Theorem 1.1.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2508.06463 — Gafni–Tao, introduction, Theorem 1.1, following remarks, and conditional asymptotic section
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — bibliography identifying the cited 1979 paper
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-23.pdf — Erdős, Some unconventional problems in number theory, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 33 (1979), especially pp. 73–74

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos682.lean — definitions and the cited proof declarations at lines 5018 and 5222

Local definition sources: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Data/Set/Density.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Nth.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Defs.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Nth.lean; Mathlib/NumberTheory/PrimeCounting.lean; Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean; Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean; Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean
review.notes: No further mathematical defects found. The main affirmative answer and solved status agree with the sources. Checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified small prime indices, the exceptional predicate as the exact negation of the good-gap predicate, harmless zero/log boundary cases, the interior small factors, and satisfiable counterexample hypotheses at d = 24. In /workspace/review/scale.lean, a kernel-checked proof shows that N/log N is not O(N/log²N), using only standard axioms. The exact linked external proof statements and density definition match the main and conditional declarations; the external project's full dependency closure was not rebuilt.

not_demonstrated.reason: The discrepancy is a nontrivial asymptotic strengthening, not a computable boundary-case failure. Refuting this Big-O estimate would already imply infinitely many exceptional prime gaps, an infinitude the cited paper leaves open. Its lower asymptotic is conditional on a prime-tuples conjecture. Showing that N/log N is not O(N/log² N) does not show that the actual exceptional count violates the asserted bound.

submission.summary: No short unconditional proof or disproof of the actual declaration was established. No trivial-proof file is retained.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported misformalization concerns the scale of an asymptotic prime-gap count. Neither finite computations nor a comparison of the two proposed error scales can prove or refute the declaration itself; doing so requires substantial additional mathematics.

submission.summary: Corrected the index-scale exceptional-count bound from O(X / (log X)^2) to O(X / log X), and updated its docstring. No other declarations were changed. The requested Lean compilation succeeds with only the existing `declaration uses sorry` warnings.
